name: CO-06
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by about 11 points
Crow has a huge money edge: $3.8M raised and $2.9M on hand versus no visible challenger funding
Incumbency plus a favorable national environment for Democrats
Prediction markets price Crow near 96% with no contrary polling
model.rationale: Every available signal points the same way: an 11-point Democratic district, a heavily funded two-term incumbent, no measurable challenger operation, and markets pricing Crow near 96%. With no polls to contradict the fundamentals, the expected margin stays close to what the district lean, environment, and money advantage imply.
model.watch: Late outside spending against Crow or a rare public poll showing a single-digit race would be the main signals that this is closer than it looks.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jason Crow, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a Colorado district that leans Democratic by about eleven points. He has raised roughly $3.8 million and holds about $2.9 million on hand, while Republican nominee Jason Clark shows no reported fundraising or outside support. Minor-party and independent candidates are on the ballot but show little financial footprint.

No public general-election polls cover the race and no expert ratings are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, money, and incumbency. Prediction markets price Crow at about 96 percent to win. The combination of a strong partisan lean, a well-funded incumbent, and a challenger with no visible resources places this race firmly in the Safe Democratic column, though the absence of polling leaves some uncertainty around the exact margin.
